label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 1 — Field markings (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: Touchlines are the long boundaries; goal lines are the short boundaries. The halfway line separates the halves. The centre mark and surrounding circle are at midfield. Each goal has a smaller goal area and a larger penalty area. The penalty mark is inside the penalty area; the penalty arc is outside it. Corner areas are quarter-circles beside corner flags. Boundary lines are part of their areas. Standard adult measurements must not be assumed for modified youth fields. Goals must be firmly secured. Play stops for a broken crossbar until repaired; if repair is impossible the match is abandoned.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 11 — Offside (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: Position is assessed when a teammate plays or touches the ball (at release for a goalkeeper throw). An attacker is in an offside position only in the opponents' half, nearer their goal line than both the ball and second-last opponent. Head, body and feet count; hands and arms do not. Being level is onside. Position alone is not an offence: involvement by playing the ball, interfering with an opponent or gaining an advantage from a rebound, deflection or save is required. There is no offside offence from receiving a goal kick, throw-in or corner directly. Offside is punished with an indirect free kick where the offence happens. An opponent?s controlled deliberate play can remove the earlier offside restriction, but a deliberate save does not; a deflection alone does not reset offside.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 12 — Fouls, cards and goalkeepers (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: Direct-kick offences include careless, reckless or excessively forceful trips, kicks, pushes and challenges, holding, and handball offences. Not all arm contact is handball. Dangerous play without contact and impeding without contact are indirect-kick examples. Yellow is a caution; red is a sending-off. Reckless challenges require yellow; excessive force or endangering an opponent requires red. A second caution means dismissal. Goalkeepers have ordinary handling restrictions outside their own penalty area. Inside it, they cannot handle again after releasing possession before another player touches it, or handle a deliberate teammate kick or direct teammate throw-in, unless they clearly kicked or attempted to kick to release it into play. Deliberate tricks to evade that restriction are offences. Holding the ball beyond eight seconds gives a corner, with a visible final-five-second countdown. Handball includes deliberate handling or an arm position making the body unnaturally bigger without justification from the player?s movement. The context of the movement matters. Shielding a ball within playing distance is legal if opponents are not held off. Safe bicycle kicks are allowed. Spitting is a sending-off offence and deliberate verbal distraction is cautionable. Recklessness does not require intent. For an offence while the ball is out, the existing restart normally remains.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 13 — Free kicks (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: Direct free kicks can score straight into the opponents' goal. Indirect free kicks need a touch by another player for a goal; the referee signals them with a raised arm until another player touches the ball, it goes out, or a direct goal is no longer possible. A restart taker touching the ball again before anyone else normally gives an indirect free kick; handball offences have separate sanctions. Free-kick location has exceptions, including attacking indirect kicks for offences inside the opponents' goal area. Players must wait if the referee has required a whistle before the restart.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 5 ? Referee authority and safety (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: The referee may allow advantage when the non-offending team benefits, returning to the original offence if the expected benefit does not develop within a few seconds. Serious injury requires stopping play. Slight injury may be handled at the next stoppage. Re-entry after injury requires the appropriate permission; bleeding must have stopped and equipment be clear of blood. Restart decisions generally cannot be changed after play restarts, or after ending a half and leaving the field, or abandoning the match. The referee can stop, suspend or abandon for serious outside interference.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 14 ? Penalty procedure (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: The goalkeeper stays on the goal line until the kick; at the moment of the kick part of one foot must touch, align with, or be behind that line. The referee signals the penalty after players are positioned. The kick goes forward. Feinting during the run-up is allowed; pretending to kick after finishing the run-up is an offence. Penalty procedures and sanctions have exceptions that require the complete law.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 15 ? Throw-ins (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: The team opposing the last player to touch the ball takes the throw-in when the whole ball crosses the touchline. Both hands deliver it from behind and over the head; part of each foot is on the line or ground outside it. A throw directly into the opponents? goal gives a goal kick; directly into the thrower?s own goal gives a corner. Normal incorrect throws go to the other team, subject to competition modifications. At release both feet must meet the ground-and-line condition, but no flat-foot, uncrossed or side-by-side stance is required. Running approaches or a prior somersault can be legal. Opponents keep 2 metres (2 yards) away; unfair distraction is cautionable and, after the throw, gives an indirect kick. A proper throw bouncing outside before entering is retaken by the same team. Official FAQs allow advantage after an incorrect throw enters and the opponents benefit. No minimum travel distance is prescribed; a drop is not a throw.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 16 ? Goal kicks (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: A goal kick is in play once kicked and clearly moving; it need not leave the penalty area. Opponents stay outside that area until it is in play, subject to quick-restart exceptions. A stationary ball is kicked from within the goal area unless competition modifications apply. A kicker?s second touch before another player touches the ball is generally an indirect-kick offence; handball has separate consequences. A defending outfield player can take the kick. It can score directly against the opponents; directly into the kicker?s own goal gives a corner.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 17 ? Corners (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: A corner can score directly into the opponents? goal. A corner is awarded when the whole ball crosses the goal line, last touched by a defender, without a goal. The ball is stationary in the nearest corner area and is in play when kicked and clearly moving. The flag is not moved. A second touch by the taker before another player normally gives an indirect kick, with separate handball consequences. Part of the stationary ball may touch or overhang the corner-area boundary. Opponents stay ten yards from the arc until the kick clearly moves. The kick may travel in any direction.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 2 ? Defective ball (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: A defective ball in open play requires stopping, replacement and a dropped ball. Defects at a restart normally require retaking that restart; penalties have specific in-flight retake conditions. The referee controls ball replacement.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 3 ? Player entry (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: Ordinary substitutes enter during a stoppage at halfway after the replaced player leaves and the referee signals. Competition return-substitution rules may modify this. Goalkeeper changes require informing the referee and a stoppage. Temporarily leaving as part of a playing movement is not automatically an offence. Team officials interfering on the field have specific disciplinary and restart provisions.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 4 ? Equipment safety (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: Dangerous equipment is prohibited. Shin guards and footwear are compulsory. Safe sports spectacles and goalkeeper caps are permitted; other headgear must meet safety conditions. Accidentally lost footwear must be replaced promptly, no later than the next stoppage; an intervening play or goal may remain valid. General IFAB jewellery restrictions are subject here to the cited PDSA local modification.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 8 ? Dropped-ball procedure (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: A dropped ball restarts play stopped by the referee when no other restart applies. Recipient and location depend on the adopted law and the circumstances, including the penalty area, ball location and possession. Do not assume a generic recipient or location.

label: IFAB 2025/26 Law 9 ? Ball status (summary)
text: Summary checked against the official 2025/26 page: The ball is out when it wholly crosses a boundary or the referee stops play. Rebounds off a goalpost, crossbar or corner flag remain live if within the field. Referee contact while the ball remains in play requires a dropped ball if a promising attack, direct goal or possession change results; other contacts normally allow play to continue.
